item.title: Aisha Buhari reveals ex-president’s cause of death, ‘final days’
item.description: Former First Lady, Aisha Buhari, has disclosed that the late former President Muhammadu Buhari died of pneumonia and not cancer. Mrs Buhari disclosed this while recounting her husband’s final days on earth. Buhari died mid 2025 in London Clinic and was flown back to Nigeria where he was buried in his hometown, Daura, Katsina State. item.title: 2027: Senator Abaribe gives conditions for defecting to APC
item.description: Senator Enyinnaya Abaribe, representing Abia South Senatorial District, has outlined stringent conditions under which he would consider defecting to the All Progressives Congress, APC. item.title: NCAA issues aerodrome certificates to Kano, Port Harcourt airports
item.description: The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) has issued aerodrome certificates to the Malam Aminu International Airport in Kano, and the Jeremiah Obafemi Awolowo International Airport, Port Harcourt. According to NAN, the certificates were presented on Friday in Abuja by Chris Najomo, director-general of the NCAA. item.title: Police to NBA: Tinted glass permit not revenue-driven, payments handled by CBN-licensed platform
item.description: The Nigeria Police Force (NPF) has rejected claims by the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) that the motor vehicle tinted glass permit policy is a revenue-generating scheme. In a statement on Friday, Benjamin Hundeyin, the force spokesperson, said the police are not a revenue-generating agency but are legally permitted to receive funds incidental to the discharge of their statutory duties. item.title: AFCON to hold every four years from 2028 as CAF floats Nations League
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has announced that the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) will be held every four years after the 2028 edition. The new development was announced at a press conference by Patrice Motsepe, CAF president, after its executive committee meeting in Morocco on Saturday — the eve of AFCON 2025.
